model_annotations.Bulgarian: This bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity for two categories, Per-Output and Per-Layer. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, labeled with percentages ranging from 10% to 80% in increments of 10%, with a linear scale. The vertical axis represents perplexity, labeled with values from 10^1 to 10^3 on a logarithmic scale. The Per-Output category is represented by blue bars, while the Per-Layer category is represented by orange bars. The bars for both categories increase in height as the sparsity rate increases, with the Per-Layer bars generally having similar or slightly higher values than the Per-Output bars. At 10%, the Per-Output bar is approximately 4 and the Per-Layer bar is approximately 3.5. At 80%, the Per-Output bar is approximately 600 and the Per-Layer bar is approximately 1000. The bars are not sorted in any specific order, but they are visually arranged in order of increasing sparsity rate. No bars are visually emphasized, but the two categories are differentiated by color.
